103	- **Issue-lifecycle floor — gate the DAG advance (§4.1).** Before advancing the DAG past this phase, run `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/war/assets/assert-issues-filed.sh assert <ledger.json> <phase-id>` (it runs `gh-preflight.sh` itself first, so an account flip cannot fake its exit). It confirms the ledger's `epic_issue` and every `tasks[].issue` exist on live `gh`, and — on a phase being **landed** — that the epic is `state:CLOSED` **and** carries `status:done`. **Route by exit code:** `0` ⇒ verified, advance; `1` ⇒ blocks the advance, surfacing the named route (`issues-missing` naming the missing/null issue, or `done-but-open`) — treat as an escalation to resolve before proceeding; `2` ⇒ a gh/network/ledger-parse **tooling error**, escalate as such, **never a silent pass** (exit 2 never collapses into 1). On a **landed** phase, close the epic via the floor's atomic mode — `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/war/assets/assert-issues-filed.sh --close-epic <n> --sha <sha>` (one call does `+status:done` / `−status:in-progress` **and** `gh issue close --reason completed` with the landed-SHA comment) — **instead of** separate label/close commands, so `status:done` can never outlive an open epic.
104	- **Follow-up filing floor — gate the DAG advance (D4, #1331).** Before advancing the DAG past a handoff-emitting phase (`landed` / `held:escalation`), every `handoff.followUps[]` entry must carry a **non-null `issue`** — the Workflow's `file-followups` dispatch normally stamps them (**consolidation precedes filing**: the engine collapses duplicate rows into `seats[]`-corroborated candidates pre-dispatch and asserts the returned `clusters[]` manifest — canonical: `FOLLOWUP_FILING_RESULT` in `assets/workflow-template.js`); any null ⇒ file it **now**, in a gh-write of its own (this floor fires at the Checkpoint, after the per-phase gh-write batch has closed, so run `gh-preflight.sh` for this write), **under the same discipline** — one issue per root cause, an open `war-followup` match gets a **corroboration comment**, never a new issue — and stamp the number into the ledger's phase `handoff` record. **Never advance over a null `issue`.**
105	- **Ask ruling gate — the strike list, gate the DAG advance absolutely (#1550, ADR 0013 amendment).** When `handoff.asks[]` is non-empty, **one gate rules all parked asks in a single pass**: render the strike list — one row per ask, its `question` + `fork` (the decision needed and its two branches) + task/seat/sha provenance, plus, on a citation-matched row, its `citationPrefill` (the engine's matched standing row + match rationale + executed sha + recommended ruling, #1879): the operator confirms or overrules in one stroke — never auto-unparked past a present operator, and a confirm-via-prefill is recorded as a citation-informed ruling in the same telemetry channel as an `--afk` citation resolution (the aced record's citation stamp) — and put it to the operator with the phase report. The advance floor is **absolute**: never advance the DAG over an unruled ask — interactively this binds as a hard wait (the run does not proceed until every row carries a ruling; no severity, count, or staleness exception). **Ruled-ask execution (ADR 0013 amendment 2026-08-27):** a ruled ask whose fix is fully specified **executes in this run** — injected into the next phase's decompose as a small first-class task carrying the ruling and its `suggested_fix`, or, in the final phase, ONE bounded polish-style post-land dispatch at the working tip. **Ruled-ask filing parity** is now filing-on-non-execution: file an issue **only** on **cannot-execute** (no vehicle, cross-task, budget) or execution-failure (regression ⇒ revert), the ruling recorded in it either way — never silently, never as default litter; when filed, it files Lead-side in a gh-write of its own, executed after this gate's ruling (the per-phase gh-write batch has already closed, so run `gh-preflight.sh` for this write), under the same discipline as engine-filed follow-ups — one issue per root cause carrying an `## Evidence artifacts` section, dedup-checked first against the engine-filed `handoff.followUps[]` rows and open `war-followup` issues (a match gets a corroboration comment, never a duplicate) — and mint each ruling as an adjudication row (the third producer, Decompose step 5) in **standing-row format** (today's ruling is tomorrow's `--afk` citation source), recorded in the ledger and threaded to every subsequent phase. # Touched-doc accuracy — the guard / de-mirror / defer trichotomy

**The duty.** A task whose slice rewrites a doc owns the factual accuracy of what it renders
authoritative. Every fact in that doc derivable from a **machine-readable in-repo source** — a config
default, a manifest field, an enum member, a version slot — takes exactly one of three lawful
treatments. Silence (restating the fact with none of the three) is a plan defect, never a follow-up.
General prose claims are out of scope — the duty binds only what a machine-readable source can
re-derive; prose claims stay governed by the evidence-tag discipline (D4).

## The trichotomy

1. **Guard** — a drift test binds the doc value to its canonical source by **extraction + equality**
   (never presence). Exemplars: `skills/war/assets/version-slots.test.mjs` (the four release slots in
   lock-step, README `## Status` included) and `skills/war/assets/war-config.test.mjs`'s frontmatter
   guard (doc-stated defaults extracted and compared against the live `DEFAULTS` export). The guard
   lands in the **same task** as the doc rewrite, or takes a `deps` edge onto it when file-disjointness
   forces a split (authoring rule 7).
2. **De-mirror** — rewrite the doc to **point at the canonical source** instead of restating its value
   ("the default is `run.roundLimit` in `war-config.mjs`", never "the default is 3"). A pointed-at fact
   cannot rot; prefer this wherever the reader does not need the literal value inline.
3. **Explicitly defer** — a **legitimacy-complete** row in the plan's
   `## Deferred validations (backstops)` section: the check, a named runner, and the timing. This is
   ADR 0017's vehicle — a validation in neither the gate, a floor, nor the backstops section may not be
   waived in prose.

## Who enforces it

- **Authoring:** `/war-strategy` §3's authoring rule 8 (`skills/war-strategy/SKILL.md` — the canonical
  statement); `/war-machine`'s drafter consumes it by reference.
- **Validation:** `/red-team`'s `touched-doc-fact-coverage` drift-guard spine probe — Lead-run prose
  like its three siblings — flags a silent restatement as a plan defect (`needsDecision`).
- **Execution backstop:** `/war`'s decompose step carries the pointer to this file, so a Lead staging a
  doc-rewriting task can check the choice was made before dispatch.
- **Audit:** a doc fact deterministically re-derivable from a machine-readable in-repo source is
  mechanical for absorb-eligibility purposes (the clarification lives in
  `skills/war/references/disposition-eligibility.md`, the eviction destination the auditor's
  standing card points at).

(plan line 107, PIN-15 / End state 7). The plan never bounds which WAR invocation modes it sanctions.
findings.reality: /war DOES have an inter-phase operator halt — `## Checkpoint (between phases)` in skills/war/SKILL.md:101: 'Post a phase report … and **wait for the user's go**.' That mechanism satisfies PIN-15 for a default interactive dispatch, so option (a) is partly true and must be named. But the same line continues: 'Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed.' An `--afk` run therefore advances the DAG from Phase 2 straight into Post-Implementation Phase 3 with no operator installation and no first installed Codex attempt on record — the exact silent continuation plan line 107 forbids, and it is unrecoverable for the experiment (Phase 3 reveals the ledger and adapts, destroying the blinded first-attempt evidence PIN-8/PIN-15/B1 exist to preserve). There is no phase bound to fall back on: the Quick start surface (skills/war/SKILL.md:14) is `/war <plan-file> [--working <branch>] [--landing <branch>] [--campaign-ordinal <K>] [--afk] [--ace] [--config <path>]` — no `--phase`, `--stop-after`, or `--until`; a repo-wide grep for `--stop-after|--phase\b|--phases|stopAfter|--until` under skills/war/ returns only assert-issues-filed.sh's `--close-epic … [--phase <label>]` epic-label argument, which is unrelated to run bounding. The plan's own statement that 'the operator intends implementation in another task using goal/Snipe, not automatic WAR dispatch' (plan line 105) is an intent note, not a constraint — it sits three lines above a clause that explicitly instructs how to dispatch this plan through WAR, so it does not close the hole (option (c) is insufficient on its own).
findings.evidence: skills/war/SKILL.md:101 — '## Checkpoint (between phases)\nPost a phase report … and **wait for the user's go**. Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed. **Hard escalations (audit-blocked, unresolvable conflict, plan-contradiction) always halt regardless of mode.**' (a PIN-15 checkpoint is none of those three hard-escalation classes). skills/war/SKILL.md:14 — flag list with no phase bound. `grep -rn -- '--stop-after|--phase\b|--phases|stopAfter|--until' skills/war/` → only assert-issues-filed.sh:18,103,110 (`--close-epic <n> --sha <sha> [--phase <label>]`) plus its test; no run-bounding flag exists. Plan lines 105, 107, 111 as quoted.
findings.fix: Settle it in the plan (more than one non-equivalent resolution — operator's call): (i) amend the WAR-dispatch clause at plan line 111 to state that WAR may be dispatched for Phases 1–2 ONLY and NEVER with `--afk`, since /war's sole inter-phase halt is the interactive `## Checkpoint (between phases)` wait and `--afk` converts it to a post-and-proceed — naming that mechanism explicitly so the Lead does not have to infer it; or (ii) split Post-Implementation Phase 3 into its own plan file so no single WAR run can contain both sides of the checkpoint; or (iii) state outright that WAR dispatch of this plan is unsanctioned and delete the conditional testPattern recipe, leaving goal/Snipe as the only implementation vehicle. Whichever is chosen, name the Checkpoint mechanism (or the split) so PIN-15 rests on something mechanical rather than on prose a Lead may narrate past.
findings.planRef: Build order (for /war) — 'Required checkpoint after Phase 2' (plan lines 105, 107, 111); PIN-15; End state 7
